checked_scope: A complete fixed-time squared-error rate for the deterministic Lipschitz-drift Bernoulli subexperiment with constant known assignment probability, together with an honest-confidence-interval lower bound at the stationary null. This is not a solution for arbitrary adaptive targets or a sharp time-uniform confidence sequence.
checks: Projection, score variance at most 1/q, and window bias L(h-1)/2 give (2); h=min(t,ceil((qL^2)^(-1/3))) satisfies h-1<=u, including t=1, L=0, q=1 and capped-risk regimes.

The observed-data KL is q times the Bernoulli KL sum, bounded by (16q/3) times squared mean differences. Nearest-target testing gives d^2(1-TV)/8; both the stationary and terminal-ramp alternatives satisfy the parameter and drift constraints.

The ramp bound q sum a_s^2<=32^-2+32^-3 makes KL<1/50 and TV<1/10. Under the stationary null, coverage of both targets has probability >=2/5 for alpha<=1/4; multiplying by d gives exactly the stated 1/80 diameter constant.

The maximum of the stationary and drift lower bounds dominates half the capped sum. The consistency equivalence follows from this two-sided rate. The earlier full manuscript supplies window upper bounds, not this matching Lipschitz lower rate or stationary-null honesty obstruction.
